What is the slowest motion detectable by the human eye?
I suggest going to the post office and time the clerks there.
Find an analog clock, and lean in real close. You can only barely make out the hour hand moving round, given a typical length of hour hand.

And as for what the 'part of the brain' is involved, your retinas actually are the first part of your brain to pick up directly on motion in your vision. You might not realize that retinas are part of your brain, but they're made of neurons. And then those neurons trigger other neurons in the optic nerve to reach the main bulk of the brain. So when you see things, light actually hits your 'brain' directly.

Doesn't this boil down to "pixels"? Slow motion = very small changes in what you're looking at. And in order to see very small changes, you have to be able to see very small things. I imagine for example that an owl would be able to see slow motions better than a human since an owl can see smaller things.
